memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'No one outside a priest's family may eat the sacred offering, nor
may the guest of a priest or his hired worker eat it. But if a priest
buys a slave with money, or if slaves are born in his household, they
may eat his food. If a priest's daughter marries anyone other than a
priest, she may not eat any of the sacred contributions'"
- Lev 22:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The line here is not wealth, status or ability. It is household. A paid
worker who came daily could not eat. A servant who genuinely belonged
to the household could. The question was never how useful you were.
The question was whether you belonged.

That is a striking picture, and it reaches straight into the gospel.
Jesus told a parable where the hired workers stood outside while sons
sat at the table. John writes that to all who received Him, He gave the
right to become children of God (John 1:12). Paul says we did not
receive a spirit that makes us slaves to fear again, but the Spirit of
adoption, by whom we cry, "Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15).

Dear reader, many believers live like hired workers. They serve
faithfully but anxiously, always wondering whether they have done
enough to stay in favour. That is not the relationship God offers.

You are not on the payroll. You are in the family. Your place at the
table was secured by Christ's blood, not by your performance.

Come and eat as a child, not as an employee.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I relate to God more like a hired worker or like a child?
2. What anxiety about "earning" my place needs to be surrendered?
3. How does adoption change the way I pray?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You have made me part of Your family through
Jesus. Free me from serving You out of fear, and let me live as Your
child. Amen.
